dossier.public_summary: The dips alternate between shallow and deep and change dramatically from sector to sector, with a few transits 1000+ ppm deep implying the source is not a small planet on this star. With centroid inconclusive and nearby stars able to mimic the signal, the best explanation is a diluted or blended eclipsing binary folded to this period.

reasons.why: Significant odd/even depth difference indicates alternating transits of different depth, expected for an eclipsing binary at twice the 12.7d period, not a planet. Sector_oe_max_sigma 6.083 with sector_oe_sectors_over_3 1 confirms.
reasons.value: 4.344 (odd 294.1 ppm vs even 494.4 ppm, depth_difference 200.3 ppm ratio 1.7, red_noise 1.179)

reasons.why: Depth changes by much more than measurement error and not just between pipelines, inconsistent with a planet on target which has a fixed depth. SPOC shows 1585 ppm in one sector versus ~5 ppm in another from same source.
reasons.value: 6.271e-58 (depth_change_pct 471.5), sector_depths_by_source verdict changes_within_a_source: SPOC 2-min p_constant 5.293906928058921e-46 (sector 100 depth_ppm 1585 err 88 vs sector 99 depth_ppm 5 err 70 and sector 101 depth_ppm 375 err 48); TESS-SPOC p_constant 0.03415781621124178)

reasons.why: Individual transit depths are wildly inconsistent, driven by a few anomalously deep events, so signal is not a repeating planet transit but variable/bleach-contaminated dips.

Centroid cannot place signal on target, and there are multiple close Gaia stars capable of producing the observed dip with <=25% eclipses, consistent with a blended neighbour EB rather than an on-target planet.
reasons.value: centroid verdict inconclusive (no sector with a clear difference image, diff_snr 0.685), neighbours plausible_within_1px 2, could_cause_within_1px 4, closest that could sep_arcsec 5.3 delta_mag 3.5 eclipse_needed 0.0105

reasons.why: Independent planet classifier ranks this highly planet-unlike, supporting the EB/blend interpretation.
